# From TUCF to Tufts HPC and Tufts Box!

## Connect to FTP to Pull Data

First, we need to connect to the FTP server

```
ftp://tucf-data.med.tufts.edu
```

Chuck's Username and Password facilitate access.

MacOS makes this process simple with a user interface that facilitates drag-and-drop.

## Connect to Tufts HPC

To connect to the HPC, we need to be on the Tufts VPN (connect using AnyConnect). Then, we can SSH in:

```

```

Once on the cluster, it can be helpful to activate conda, your virtual environment, and move to the `/code` directory.

```
module load anaconda/2021.05
source activate /cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/condaenv/vhh
cd /cluster/tufts/cowenlab/$USER/code
```


## Compress data after pulling down, push to Tufts HPC

### Compress

Before we push the data to the Tufts HPC, we will compress it with the following general command.

```
tar -czvf [output_name.tar.gz] [input_folder]
```

```
tar -czvf 240815_0062_Shoemaker_8265.tar.gz 240815_0062_Charles_Shoemaker-8265
```

### Securely Copy Illumina Data to Cluster

Now, we securely copy the data up to the cluster with the general command:

```
scp -r [local_path_to_folder] [path_to_cluster_folder]
```

*Note:* This command must be run from the machine that has the file/folder.

```
scp -r ~/VHH/data/240815_0062_Shoemaker_8265.tar.gz emosel01@xfer.cluster.tufts.edu:/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/
```

Once uploaded, we navigate to the `/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/$USER/data` directory and decrompress the data with the following command:

```
tar -xzvf 240815_0062_Shoemaker_8265.tar.gz
```

We ensure there exist folders that are properly populated according to our desired Global Set definitions:

* Global Set: `XLI` - Experiments 1 - 15
* Global Set: `JPL-1` - Experiments 16 - 20
* Global Set: `XIV-3` - Experiments 21 - 27
* Global Set: `JGW-2` - Experiments 28 - 34

We use the commands in the `/data` directory to make subdirectories which will hold our experiments for global clustering:

```
mkdir XLI
mkdir JPL
mkdir XIV
mkdir JGW
```

We then move to the `fastq_Lane1` folder in the file containing the Illumina run data, 

```
cd 240815_0062_Shoemaker_8265/fastq_Lane1/
```

We then delete the following unnecessary files within the `fastq_Lane1` directory:

```
rm *.html
rm *.zip
rm Undetermined_S0_L001*
```

**Note:** `Undetermined` sequences lack a barcode, so we consider them impossible to assign to an experiment.

This leaves the paired-end read files, which need to be decompressed:

```
gunzip *
```

We then move experiments to their Global Set directories which we made earlier in the `/data` directory.

**Note:** we can also simply leave the data in this directory, and treat the entire Illumina run as its own global set.

```
[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv [1-9]_* ../../XLI
[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv 1[0-5]_* ../../XLI

[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv 1[6-9]_* ../../JPL
[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv 20_* ../../JPL

[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv 2[1-7]_* ../../XIV

[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv 2[8-9]_* ../../JGW
[emosel01@login-prod-01 fastq_Lane1]$ mv 3[0-4]_* ../../JGW
```

At any point, we can run `ls ../../JGW` to see which files exist in the folder we are moving them to.

## Assembly

Now, we ensure that the `VHHAssembly.sh` script points to the correct `DATA_BIN` path:

```
vim VHHAssembly.sh
```

Now we ensure that the input data is pointing to the right directory by adjusting the `DATA_BIN` variable near the top of `VHHAssembly.sh`:

```
# Define environmental variables

PRESTO_BIN=/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/immcantation_suite/presto/bin
CHANGEO_BIN=/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/immcantation_suite/changeo/bin
NCBI_BIN=/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/ncbi-igblast-1.22.0/bin

OUT_BIN=/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/240520_0044_Charles_Shoemaker-8125/fastq_Lane1
DATA_BIN=/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/240520_0044_Charles_Shoemaker-8125/fastq_Lane1
```

Note that both pRESTO and Change-O are installed in the `/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/` directory, so we are using Prof. Cowen lab's installation to assemble our reads.


To exit `vim`, first `esc`, then write with `:w`, then quit with `:q`. If you'd prefer not to write your changes, first `esc`, then enter `:q!`.

Now we send the script as a batch to slurm with:

```
sbatch VHHAssembly.sh
```

### Output

The following files will be created for each set of paired-end reads, and they will be deposited in the `DATA_BIN` folder (with their original paired-end read files).

```

-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab   91698889 Aug 20 19:07 34_S34_atleast-1.fasta
-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab  163815479 Aug 20 19:07 34_S34_atleast-1.fastq

-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab  163815479 Aug 20 19:07 34_S34_collapse-unique.fastq
-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab   26574841 Aug 21 02:01 34_S34_db-fail.tsv
-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab  351509479 Aug 21 02:01 34_S34_db-pass.tsv
-rwx------ 1 emosel01 cowenlab  218850464 Aug 19 14:58 34_S34_L001_R1_001.fastq
-rwx------ 1 emosel01 cowenlab  218850464 Aug 19 14:58 34_S34_L001_R2_001.fastq
```

Many of these are unimportant, so can be removed:

```
rm *MPC*
rm *MPV*
rm *quality*
rm *under*
rm *collapse*
rm *quality*
rm *assemble*
```

We proceed with the `[Prefix]_db-pass.tsv` file, in this case `34_S34_db-pass.tsv`.

The following log files will appear in the `./code` directory (the working directory):

```
-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab   1274 Aug 20 19:55 assembly.7175749.d1cmp037.err
-rw-rw---- 1 emosel01 cowenlab 144539 Aug 20 19:55 assembly.7175749.d1cmp037.out
```

These data can be parsed, so the losses can be determined at any given assembly operation (quality filtering, primer trimming, IgBLAST, etc.).

## Hierarchical Clustering

We rely on `HierarchicalClustering.R` to perform this operation. We provide the program with information on the location of all `.tsv` files which should be included in the clustering, the program aggregates the sequence information, translates to VHHs, and any VHH with 2 or more observations will be allowed to remain in the Global Set.

Now, we define the root directory, which in this case contains all relevant data, and we name the output file.

**Note:** Naming conventions continue to evolve, but using `GS_` as a prefix for the global set is a convenient heuristic.

```
# Set root dir
root_dir <- "/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/Schisto/"

output_file <- paste0(root_dir, "GS_Schisto_d2VHH_21Aug24_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv")
```

After clustering, we can look at the `tail` of the log files to see where our file is written:

```
(/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/condaenv/vhh) [emosel01@login-prod-03 code]$ tail -n 1 hclust.7379948.d1cmp004.*
==> hclust.7379948.d1cmp004.err <==
Running defineClonesScoper in bulk mode and only keep heavy chains

==> hclust.7379948.d1cmp004.out <==
Writing:  /cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/Schisto/GS_Schisto_d2VHH_21Aug24_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv 
```

## CleanCluster

We now populate the `CleanCluster.R` script with the appropriate file paths:

```
# CleanCluster Algorithm

## Change Library path to ensure we have access
.libPaths("/cluster/tufts/hpc/tools/R/4.3.0")
## Load Libraries
source("/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/code/lib/utilities.R")

## Draw file info from commandArgs
args <- c("GS_Schisto_d2VHH_21Aug24_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv")

# Define root_path
root_path <- "/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/Schisto/"
```

Here, we specifically want to define `args` as the global set file, and the `root_path` should point to the folder that the global set is in. Note that this will be the same folder that all component data sets are in.

**Note:** mmseqs2 will create database files in the `tmp` folder, which is created in the global set directory. These aren't particularly useful to us, and can be removed.

## Abundance tabulation

Abundance tabulation is performed by editing the path and global set information in `Abundance.R`.

```
root_dir <- "/cluster/tufts/cowenlab/emosel01/data/JGW/"

file_name <- "GS_JGW_d2VHH_21Aug24-cleaned-GS.csv"

files <- list.files(root_dir)[grepl("-pass.tsv", list.files(root_dir))]

GS_name <- list.files(root_dir)[grepl("GS", list.files(root_dir))]
```
